text.id: Enter deep learning. This research project, developed at BINUS University, was built to figure out the absolute most effective way to teach an AI to spot Alzheimer's. The goal wasn't just to build a model, but to systematically evaluate how different spatial representations of the brain impact an algorithm's diagnostic power.

text.id: With the global population aging rapidly, neurodegenerative conditions like Alzheimer's Disease (AD) are becoming one of the most critical healthcare challenges of our generation. While there is currently no absolute cure, early detection is everything. But diagnosing the subtle structural changes in the brain during the early stages of cognitive decline is incredibly difficult, often requiring a highly trained clinical eye.

text.id: To train a heavy-hitting medical AI, you need flawless data. The project relied on raw 1.5T MRI scans sourced directly from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI).

project relied on raw 1.5T MRI scans sourced directly from the

text.id: Rather than feeding the AI the entire brain and hoping it figured things out, the research pipeline aggressively cropped the data down to a highly specific Region of Interest (ROI): the hippocampus. Because Alzheimer's is notoriously linked to the severe shrinking (atrophy) of the hippocampus and the enlargement of the ventricles, forcing the model to hyper-focus on this specific anatomy bridged the gap between raw data and actual clinical relevance.
